The capacity of each stream in the RO-DM plant (as well as individual equipment) is designed to produce the required output quantity and includes the additional requirement of DM water for regeneration purposes/backwash of exchangers. RO permeated water is fed to the Mixed Bed Exchangers. DM water is stored in a DM water storage tank and pumped to the consumers. DM water pipework is terminated at a pressure at the take-over points for distribution to various consumers. Complete operation of the plant (including chemical and wastewater) is fully automatic. Provision is kept in the system to operate all streams of RO modules, exchangers, and all the related stand-by pumps through HMI as well as manually to meet peak/ emergency requirements. The standby unit is available for emergency requirements (plant filling), maintenance, resin replacement, etc. The treatment plant is designed considering 24-hour continuous operation (backwash once in 22 hours for Dual media filter). The mixed bed unit is regenerated once in 96 hours. The preliminary lakewater quality received from Cliff’s Burns harbor plant does not report any turbidity and TSS (Total suspended solids). Therefore, UF system has not been considered in the design. If turbidity and TSS are high in the future, a UF system will be required, and the same can be added later. Presently, inlet TSS is assumed as 10 ppm for designing the pre-treatment of the RO-DM plant. 7.2.2 Water Quality The makeup water quality as received from the plant is shown in Table 22, and the expected water quality from DM plant is shown in Table 23.
